title: the read copied the payload's length into a caller buffer sized by the caller
consumer: libavformat/librist.c, librist_read's copy into the caller's buffer
object: the caller's read buffer, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a copy sized by the SOURCE payload instead of the destination buffer
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real shape: the copy length is taken from the source, as upstream's was.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavformat/librist.c carries `size = FFMIN(data_block->payload_len, size);`. The pre-fix form, `size = data_block->payload_len;`, is at 8880a174d0^ and is absent from the pin.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x10226e, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x102256` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

native-detect.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner allocator between, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the classic destination-vs-source sizing error, and the only row here where the overrun length is the SOURCE's size rather than a fixed offset or a stream-declared length.
